questions.question: A North Carolina learner permit is available to persons who are:
choices: at least 15 years old and under 18
at least 16 years old and under 18
questions.explanation: Learner permits are available to persons age 18 and older. Drivers under 18 follow the graduated licensing levels.
questions.sourceQuote: Learner permits are available to persons age 18 and older.

questions.question: While driving with a learner permit, the permit holder must be accompanied by:
choices: any passenger who is at least 21 years old
a parent or guardian seated in the back seat
a licensed driver following in another vehicle
a licensed driver seated beside the permit holder
questions.explanation: The accompanying driver must be licensed to operate the motor vehicle being driven and must be seated beside the permit holder.
questions.sourceQuote: be accompanied by a person who is licensed to operate the motor vehicle being driven and is seated beside the permit holder.

questions.question: The on-the-road driving test is required for an original license, but:
choices: it is required for a learner permit
it is required only for applicants under 18
it is required only if the examiner requests it
it is not required for a learner permit
questions.explanation: Applicants for an original driver license must take the on-the-road test, but it is not required for a learner permit.
questions.sourceQuote: It is not required for a learner permit.

questions.question: To apply for a Level One Limited Learner Permit you must be at least:
questions.explanation: You must be at least 15 years old but less than 18 years old and reside in North Carolina.
questions.sourceQuote: You must be at least 15 years old but less than 18 years old and reside in North Carolina.

questions.question: The approved driver education course required before the learner permit test consists of:
choices: 20 hours of classroom instruction and 10 hours behind the wheel
30 hours of classroom instruction and 6 hours behind the wheel
30 hours of classroom instruction and 10 hours behind the wheel
6 hours of classroom instruction and 30 hours behind the wheel
questions.explanation: North Carolina requires at least 30 hours of classroom instruction and six hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.
questions.sourceQuote: consisting of at least 30 hours classroom instruction and six hours behind-the wheel instruction

questions.question: During the first six months of holding a Level One permit, you may drive:
choices: at any time, as long as a supervising driver is with you
between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m. while accompanied by your supervising driver
between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. while accompanied by your supervising driver
questions.explanation: The Level One permit allows driving between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m. during the first six months, while accompanied by the supervising driver.
questions.sourceQuote: a level one permit authorizes you to drive between the hours of 5 a.m. and 9 p.m., while accompanied by your supervising driver

questions.question: You must hold a Level One Limited Learner Permit for how long before applying for a Limited Provisional License?
questions.explanation: The permit must be held for nine months before applying for a Limited Provisional License.
questions.sourceQuote: You must hold this permit for nine months prior to applying for a Limited Provisional License.

questions.question: The Driving Log for a Level One permit must detail a minimum of:
questions.explanation: The log must show at least 60 hours of operation, with at least 10 of those hours at night.
questions.sourceQuote: detailing a minimum of 60 hours of operation. At least 10 hours must occur during nighttime hours.

questions.question: A supervising driver must have been licensed for at least:
questions.explanation: A supervising driver must hold a valid driver license and must have been licensed for at least five years.
questions.sourceQuote: A supervising driver must hold a valid driver license and must have been licensed for at least five years.

questions.question: A Level Two Limited Provisional License is available to drivers who are at least:
questions.explanation: Level Two drivers must be at least 16 years old, but less than 18.
questions.sourceQuote: Drivers must be at least 16 years old, but less than 18.

questions.question: A Level Two licensee may drive without supervision from 5 a.m. until 9 p.m. and at any time when:
choices: driving to or from any school event
driving with a passenger who is 21 or older
driving directly to or from work or any volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service
questions.explanation: Driving directly to or from work, or any volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service, is an exception to the 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. unsupervised limit.
questions.sourceQuote: at any time when driving directly to or from work or any volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service

questions.question: When driving unsupervised with a Level Two license, how many passengers under 21 who are not members of the same household may be in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: There may be one passenger under 21 who is not a member of the same household as the driver.
questions.sourceQuote: there may be one passenger that is under 21 that is not a member of the same household as the driver

questions.question: Which statement about a Level Three Full Provisional License is correct?
choices: The time of driving, supervision and passenger limits from levels one and two do not apply
The time of driving, supervision and passenger limits from levels one and two still apply
Only the passenger limit still applies
Only the nighttime driving limit still applies
questions.explanation: The restrictions on levels one and two concerning time of driving, supervision and passenger limitations do not apply to a Full Provisional License.
questions.sourceQuote: The restrictions on level one and level two concerning time of driving, supervision and passenger limitations do not apply

questions.question: For a provisional licensee, a conviction for driving after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs results in:
questions.explanation: It is unlawful for a provisional licensee to drive after consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs, and a conviction results in a one-year license revocation.
questions.sourceQuote: a conviction of such a violation will result in a one-year license revocation.

questions.question: A student who is suspended for more than 10 consecutive days, or assigned to an alternative educational setting for more than 10 consecutive days, loses driving privileges for:
questions.explanation: That loss of license remains in effect for 12 months.
questions.sourceQuote: This suspension remains in effect for 12 months.

questions.question: A first-time applicant for a North Carolina driver license, learner permit or ID card must provide proof of:
choices: full name and date of birth, NC residence address, and Social Security number or legal presence
date of birth and driving experience
questions.explanation: First-time applicants must prove their full name and date of birth, their NC residence address, and their SSN or legal presence in the U.S.
questions.sourceQuote: you will need to provide proof of your full name and date of birth, your NC residence address, proof of your Social Security number (SSN)

questions.question: A customer 18 or over applying for a driver license must show how many proofs of N.C. residency?
questions.explanation: Adults must show two proofs of N.C. residency.
questions.sourceQuote: Customers must show two proofs of N.C. residency.

questions.question: If you are not eligible for a Social Security Number, you must provide:
choices: a North Carolina voter precinct card
documents indicating your legal presence in the United States
proof of a permanent NC mailing address only
questions.explanation: Applicants who are not eligible for an SSN must provide document(s) indicating their legal presence in the United States.
questions.sourceQuote: If you are not eligible for a SSN, you must provide document(s) indicating your legal presence in the United States.

questions.question: A North Carolina REAL ID is:
choices: a driver license, learner permit or identification card with a star
a card marked NOT FOR FEDERAL IDENTIFICATION
a passport card issued by the state
questions.explanation: A REAL ID is a driver license, learner permit or identification card with a star, and it meets federal identification requirements.
questions.sourceQuote: A REAL ID is a driver license, learner permit or identification card with a star.

questions.question: A new resident has how long after establishing residence to obtain a North Carolina license or learner permit?
questions.explanation: A new resident has 60 days after establishing residence to obtain a North Carolina license or learner permit.
questions.sourceQuote: A new resident has 60 days after establishing residence to obtain a North Carolina license or learner permit.

questions.question: A driver license may be renewed anytime within how many days prior to its expiration?
questions.explanation: A driver license may be renewed anytime within 180 days prior to expiration.
questions.sourceQuote: A driver license may be renewed anytime within 180 days prior to expiration.

questions.question: To replace a lost or stolen license, you may:
choices: show the examiner two documents of identification approved by the DMV
report it to the police and wait 30 days
request the replacement by telephone only
questions.explanation: A duplicate for a lost or stolen license may be issued after you show the examiner two approved documents of identification.
questions.sourceQuote: To replace a lost or stolen license, you may show the examiner two documents of identification approved by the DMV.

questions.question: If you accumulate seven driver license points, you may be assigned to:
choices: a defensive driving course required by your insurer
questions.explanation: Seven points may result in assignment to a driver improvement clinic.
questions.sourceQuote: If you accumulate seven points, you may be assigned to a driver improvement clinic.

questions.question: Upon satisfactory completion of the driver improvement clinic:
choices: one point is deducted from your driving record
three points are deducted from your driving record
five points are deducted from your driving record
all points are removed from your driving record
questions.explanation: Three points are deducted from your driving record upon satisfactory completion of the clinic.
questions.sourceQuote: Upon satisfactory completion of the clinic, three points are deducted from your driving record.

questions.question: If you accumulate as many as 12 points within a three-year period:
choices: you receive a warning letter only
you must retake the knowledge test
questions.explanation: Twelve points within a three-year period can result in suspension of your license.
questions.sourceQuote: If you accumulate as many as 12 points within a three-year period, your license may be suspended.

questions.question: How many points within three years following reinstatement of your license can result in a second suspension?
questions.explanation: Eight points within three years following reinstatement can result in a second suspension.
questions.sourceQuote: The accumulation of eight points within three years following the reinstatement of your license can result in a second suspension.

questions.question: If your driver license is suspended by the point system, the first suspension may be for:
questions.explanation: The first point-system suspension may be for 60 days, the second for 6 months and the third for 12 months.
questions.sourceQuote: 60 days for the first suspension

questions.question: When your driving privilege is reinstated after a point suspension:
choices: all driver license points and insurance points are canceled
all previous driver license points are canceled, but insurance points are not
questions.explanation: Reinstatement cancels all previous driver license points, but this does not pertain to insurance points.
questions.sourceQuote: When your driving privilege is reinstated, all previous driver license points are canceled. This does not pertain to insurance points.

questions.question: How many driver license points are assessed for passing a stopped school bus?
questions.explanation: Passing a stopped school bus carries 5 driver license points.
questions.sourceQuote: Passing a stopped school bus 5

questions.question: How many driver license points are assessed for reckless driving?
questions.explanation: Reckless driving carries 4 driver license points.
questions.sourceQuote: Reckless driving 4

questions.question: Which of these convictions carries no driver license points?
questions.explanation: Illegal parking is one of the offenses for which no points are assessed.
questions.sourceQuote: • Illegal parking;

questions.question: Insurance companies use:
choices: a different point system to determine insurance rates
the same point system that the DMV uses
questions.explanation: Insurance companies use a different point system to determine insurance rates. Contact your insurance agent with questions.
questions.sourceQuote: Insurance companies use a different point system to determine insurance rates.

questions.question: Your driving privilege will be revoked for at least 30 days if you are convicted of driving more than how many miles per hour over the speed limit while driving at a speed higher than 55 mph?
questions.explanation: Driving more than 15 mph over the speed limit while driving at a speed higher than 55 mph brings a revocation of at least 30 days.
questions.sourceQuote: Driving any vehicle more than 15 miles per hour over the speed limit, if you are driving at a speed higher than 55 mph.

questions.question: Which conviction will result in a 60-day suspension of your driving privilege?
choices: speeding plus reckless driving on the same occasion
a single conviction of speeding 10 mph over the limit
questions.explanation: Speeding plus reckless driving on the same occasion is listed among the convictions that bring a 60-day suspension.
questions.sourceQuote: Speeding plus reckless driving on the same occasion.

questions.question: A conviction for prearranged racing with another motor vehicle on the highway results in a suspension of:
questions.explanation: Prearranged racing with another motor vehicle on the highway carries a three-year suspension.
questions.sourceQuote: Prearranged racing with another motor vehicle on the highway *3 years

questions.question: Attempting to obtain a license or learner permit under false pretense results in a suspension of:
questions.explanation: The suspension for attempting to obtain a license or learner permit under false pretense is one year.
questions.sourceQuote: Attempting to obtain a license or learner permit under false pretense 1 year

questions.question: Convictions that occur outside North Carolina:
choices: have no effect on your North Carolina driving privilege
are handled only by the other state
may result in your license being suspended or revoked just as if the violations occurred in this state
questions.explanation: Out-of-state convictions can result in your license being suspended or revoked just as if the violations occurred in this state.
questions.sourceQuote: may result in your license being suspended or revoked just as if the violations occurred in this state

questions.question: When the Division is notified that you failed to appear in court or pay court fines for a citation, what happens?
choices: your license is revoked for 30 days automatically
you must retake all license tests
you must appear at a DMV hearing within 10 days
you will be notified of the effective date of the revocation if the fines are not paid or waived in time
questions.explanation: The Division notifies you of the effective date of the revocation if the fines are not paid or waived prior to the date indicated.
questions.sourceQuote: you will be notified of the effective date of the revocation if the fines are not paid or waived

questions.question: A provisional licensee's license may be suspended for 30 days upon conviction of:
choices: a second moving violation occurring within a 12-month period
a third moving violation occurring within a 12-month period
questions.explanation: For provisional licensees under 18, a second moving violation within a 12-month period brings a 30-day suspension.
questions.sourceQuote: 30 days, upon conviction of a second moving violation occurring within a 12-month period

questions.question: A provisional licensee convicted of a fourth moving violation occurring within a 12-month period faces a suspension of:
questions.explanation: A fourth moving violation within a 12-month period brings a six-month suspension.
questions.sourceQuote: Six months, upon conviction of a fourth moving violation occurring within a 12-month period.

questions.question: How much must be paid to the DMV before a suspension or revocation can be cleared?
questions.explanation: North Carolina law requires a restoration fee of $83.50 before a suspension or revocation can be cleared.
questions.sourceQuote: a restoration fee of $83.50 be paid to the DMV before a suspension or revocation can be cleared

questions.question: A restoration fee of $167.25 is required when the revocation results from:
choices: a failure to appear in court
questions.explanation: The $167.25 restoration fee is required when the revocation results from a DWI conviction.
questions.sourceQuote: A $167.25 restoration fee is required when the revocation results from a DWI conviction.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration is everyone's driving impaired?
questions.explanation: Everyone's driving is impaired at a BAC of 0.08 percent, although many people are affected at much lower levels.
questions.sourceQuote: Everyone’s driving is impaired at a blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, of 0.08 percent

questions.question: Research shows the risk of being involved in a crash increases when the alcohol level reaches what percentage?
questions.explanation: The risk of being involved in a crash increases at 0.05 percent, and at 0.08 percent the risk of causing a fatal crash is even greater.
questions.sourceQuote: the risk of being involved in a crash increases when the alcohol level is 0.05 percent

questions.question: In what year did the North Carolina General Assembly enact the Safe Roads Act?
questions.explanation: The Safe Roads Act was enacted in 1983.
questions.sourceQuote: In 1983, the North Carolina General Assembly enacted the Safe Roads Act.

questions.question: What did the Safe Roads Act do?
choices: Lowered the legal drinking age to 18
Created the state's first commercial driver license program
Repealed all previous drunk driving laws and replaced them with a single offense of Driving While Impaired
Required ignition interlock devices on all new vehicles
questions.explanation: The act repealed all previous drunk driving laws and replaced them with one offense, Driving While Impaired, or DWI.
questions.sourceQuote: This act repealed all previous laws on drunk driving in North Carolina and replaced them with a single offense

questions.question: If an officer charges you with driving while impaired, you will be asked to take a chemical test of what?
questions.explanation: A person charged with DWI is asked to take a chemical test of their breath or blood.
questions.sourceQuote: you will be asked to take a chemical test of your breath or blood

questions.question: If you refuse to perform a required chemical test, your driver license will be revoked immediately for at least how long?
questions.explanation: Refusal to perform a required test results in immediate revocation of your driver license for at least 30 days.
questions.sourceQuote: Refusal to perform any required test will result in the immediate revocation of your driver license for at least 30 days

questions.question: Besides the immediate revocation, what additional revocation does the DMV impose for refusing a required chemical test?
questions.explanation: A refusal also brings an additional, minimum 12-month revocation by the DMV.
questions.sourceQuote: and an additional, minimum 12-month revocation by the DMV

questions.question: After how many months of the willful refusal revocation have elapsed may a judge issue a limited driving privilege?
questions.explanation: In certain instances, after six months of the willful refusal revocation has elapsed, the judge may issue a limited driving privilege.
questions.sourceQuote: after six months of the willful refusal revocation has elapsed, the judge may issue a limited driving privilege

questions.question: If your chemical test shows a BAC of 0.08 percent or more, your driving privilege will be revoked immediately for a minimum of what period?
questions.explanation: A test result of 0.08 percent or more (0.04 or more in a commercial motor vehicle) brings immediate revocation for a minimum of 30 days.
questions.sourceQuote: your driving privilege will be revoked immediately for a minimum of 30 days

questions.question: What BAC level is the impaired driving threshold when you are driving a commercial motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: For a commercial motor vehicle the threshold is 0.04 or more, lower than the 0.08 limit for other drivers.
questions.sourceQuote: 0.08 percent or more (0.04 or more, if you are driving a commercial motor vehicle)

questions.question: Besides proving a BAC of 0.08 percent or more, how else can driving while impaired be proven?
choices: By proving the driver was speeding
By proving the driver failed a road sign test
By proving the driver had an open container
By proving the driver's physical or mental fitness are appreciably impaired by alcohol, drugs, or a combination of both
questions.explanation: DWI can be proven either by impairment of the driver's physical or mental fitness by alcohol, drugs or a combination of both, or by BAC of 0.08 percent or more.
questions.sourceQuote: the driver's physical or mental fitness are appreciably impaired by alcohol, drugs or a combination of both

questions.question: What may be used as evidence in court in a DWI case?
choices: The results of your chemical test or the fact that you refused to take the test
Only statements made to the officer at the stop
questions.explanation: The results of your chemical test or the fact that you refused to take the test are admissible as evidence in court.
questions.sourceQuote: the results of your chemical test or the fact that you refused to take the test will be admissible as evidence in court

questions.question: Which practice do North Carolina DWI laws allow enforcement agencies to use?
choices: Road blocks to check for impaired drivers
Immediate vehicle forfeiture at any speeding stop
questions.explanation: DWI laws allow enforcement agencies to set up road blocks to check for impaired drivers.
questions.sourceQuote: Allow enforcement agencies to set up road blocks to check for impaired drivers

questions.question: Under North Carolina DWI laws, what are drivers prohibited from doing while driving?
choices: Consuming any alcoholic beverage, including beer
Carrying a closed container in the trunk
Having passengers who have been drinking
questions.explanation: Drivers are prohibited from consuming any alcoholic beverage, including beer, while driving.
questions.sourceQuote: Prohibit drivers from consuming any alcoholic beverage, including beer, while driving

questions.question: What does North Carolina law say about transporting an open container of an alcoholic beverage?
choices: It is prohibited, including in the passenger area of the car
It is allowed if the container is on the floor
It is allowed if the container is less than half full
It is allowed for passengers 21 and older
questions.explanation: The transport of an open container of any alcoholic beverage is prohibited, including in the passenger area of the car.
questions.sourceQuote: Prohibit the transport of an open container of any alcoholic beverage, including in the passenger area of the car

questions.question: In a commercial motor vehicle, what is prohibited in the passenger area while on any highway, street, or public vehicular area?
choices: Possession of alcoholic beverages, open or closed
Nothing; commercial vehicle rules do not cover alcohol
questions.explanation: It is against the law to possess alcoholic beverages, open or closed, in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on any highway, street, or public vehicular area.
questions.sourceQuote: Prohibit the possession of alcoholic beverages (open or closed) in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle

questions.question: What does North Carolina DWI law require of a person convicted of DWI for the second time?
choices: Installation of an ignition interlock on every family vehicle
questions.explanation: Persons convicted of DWI for the second time are required to serve a jail sentence.
questions.sourceQuote: Require persons who are convicted of DWI for the second time to serve a jail sentence

questions.question: What must anyone convicted of DWI obtain before driving privileges are reinstated?
questions.explanation: Anyone convicted of DWI must obtain a substance abuse assessment prior to the reinstatement of driving privileges.
questions.sourceQuote: Require anyone convicted of DWI to obtain a substance abuse assessment prior to the reinstatement of driving privileges

questions.question: Under North Carolina DWI laws, what are persons with lower BACs required to attend?
choices: A defensive driving clinic for commercial drivers
questions.explanation: DWI laws require persons with lower BACs to attend alcohol safety schools.
questions.sourceQuote: Require persons with lower BACs to attend alcohol safety schools

questions.question: If you are convicted of DWI while your license is revoked for an earlier DWI conviction, what may the court do?
choices: Order your vehicle seized and sold
questions.explanation: The court may order your vehicle seized and sold when you are convicted of DWI while your license is already revoked for an earlier DWI conviction.
questions.sourceQuote: the court may order your vehicle seized and sold

questions.question: What is the mandatory driver license revocation period for a first DWI conviction?
questions.explanation: A first DWI conviction brings mandatory revocation of your driver license for one year.
questions.sourceQuote: First conviction: Mandatory revocation of your driver license for a period of one year.

questions.question: A second DWI conviction brings a mandatory four-year revocation when the prior offense occurred within what period of the current offense?
questions.explanation: The four-year revocation for a second conviction applies when the prior offense occurred within three years of the current offense.
questions.sourceQuote: Mandatory driver license revocation for a period of four years when convicted of a prior offense which occurred within three years

questions.question: A third DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent license revocation if at least one prior conviction occurred within what period?
questions.explanation: A third conviction means mandatory permanent revocation if at least one of the prior convictions occurred within the past five years.
questions.sourceQuote: Mandatory, permanent driver license revocation if at least one of the prior convictions occurred within the past five years.

questions.question: A fourth DWI conviction is considered a felony if the three prior DWI convictions occurred within what period?
questions.explanation: A fourth conviction is a felony when the three prior DWI convictions occurred within the past seven years.
questions.sourceQuote: The fourth conviction is considered a felony if the three prior DWI convictions occurred within the past seven years.

questions.question: On the first restoration of a license after a DWI suspension, what is the required alcohol concentration restriction?
questions.explanation: On the first restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction is 0.04.
questions.sourceQuote: On the first restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction will be 0.04.

questions.question: What is the alcohol concentration restriction on a second or subsequent restoration after a DWI suspension?
questions.explanation: On a second or subsequent restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction is 0.00.
questions.sourceQuote: On a second or subsequent restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction will be 0.00.

questions.question: A DWI conviction with a BAC of 0.15 or more, or another conviction within the past seven years, requires what?
choices: An ignition interlock device installed on the vehicle
questions.explanation: A conviction with a BAC of 0.15 or more, or another conviction within the past seven years, requires an ignition interlock device on the vehicle.
questions.sourceQuote: 0.15 or more, or another conviction within the past seven years, will require an ignition interlock device to be installed on the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the legal age to purchase any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina?
questions.explanation: The legal age to purchase any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina is 21.
questions.sourceQuote: The legal age to purchase any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina is 21.

questions.question: A driver who is less than 21 years old and convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body will have their license revoked for what period?
questions.explanation: A driver under 21 convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body loses their license for one year.
questions.sourceQuote: is convicted for an offense of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body, their license will be revoked for one year.

questions.question: Which of the following results in a one-year driver license revocation?
choices: Giving an alcoholic beverage to an underage person
Riding as a passenger with a driver who has an open container
Allowing a 25-year-old friend to use your license
questions.explanation: The one-year revocation applies to any person who gives an alcoholic beverage to an underage person, along with several underage purchase and fraudulent ID offenses.
questions.sourceQuote: Any person who gives an alcoholic beverage to any underage person.

questions.question: Driving on the left side of the road is legal only in which situations?
choices: When you are driving a large vehicle
On any road where no one is behind you
On one-way streets and while passing
questions.explanation: The law requires you to drive on the right side of the road. Driving on the left side is legal only in some cases, such as on one-way streets and while passing.
questions.sourceQuote: Driving on the left side is legal only in some cases, such as on one-way streets and while passing.

questions.question: You are driving on a multi-lane highway slower than the posted speed limit. Which lane should you use?
choices: The lane with the least traffic
questions.explanation: When you are moving slower than the posted speed limit on a multi-lane highway, drive in the extreme right lane unless you are passing, turning left or avoiding an obstruction.
questions.sourceQuote: When you are moving slower than the posted speed limit on a multi-lane highway, drive in the extreme right lane

questions.question: Why should you keep enough distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead on the open road?
choices: So you can see road signs farther ahead
So your headlights are more visible
So a passing vehicle can safely move into and occupy the space
questions.explanation: On the open road, keep enough distance between you and the vehicle ahead so that a passing vehicle can safely move into and occupy the space.
questions.sourceQuote: keep enough distance between you and the vehicle ahead so that a passing vehicle can safely move into and occupy the space.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, why must you check over your shoulder?
choices: To see how far behind you the next car is
To be certain the blind spot is clear
To check the lane markings for a passing zone
questions.explanation: Important rules about changing lanes include checking the side and rear-view mirrors and checking over your shoulder to be certain the blind spot is clear.
questions.sourceQuote: Check over your shoulder to be certain the blind spot is clear;

questions.question: Why should you stay close to the right edge of the road when making a right turn?
choices: So you can turn without signaling
So you can speed up before the turn
So you can see traffic signals better
So another vehicle cannot move between your vehicle and the curb
questions.explanation: For right turns, stay close to the right edge of the road, so that another vehicle cannot move between your vehicle and the curb.
questions.sourceQuote: For right turns, stay close to the right edge of the road, so that another vehicle cannot move between your vehicle and the curb.

questions.question: How should you handle your speed when making a turn?
choices: Speed up before the turn and brake in the middle of it
Keep the same speed throughout the turn
Reduce speed before making the turn and then accelerate slightly
questions.explanation: Reduce the vehicle's speed before making the turn and then accelerate slightly.
questions.sourceQuote: Reduce the vehicle’s speed before making the turn and then accelerate slightly.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a curve?
choices: Brake firmly while you are in the middle of the curve
Slow down before you enter the curve so you will not need to brake in the curve
Speed up before the curve to keep your traction
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter the curve so that you will not need to brake while you are in the curve, then gradually increase your speed to maintain traction.
questions.sourceQuote: Slow down before you enter the curve so that you will not need to brake while you are in the curve;

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, how far to the left must the passing driver pass?
questions.explanation: The law requires the passing driver to pass at least two feet to the left of the vehicle being passed.
questions.sourceQuote: The law requires the passing driver to pass at least two feet to the left of the vehicle being passed.

questions.question: Passing is always unsafe and usually illegal on a curve or hill where the driver cannot see at least how far ahead?
questions.explanation: Passing is always unsafe and usually illegal on any curve or hill where the driver cannot see at least 500 feet ahead.
questions.sourceQuote: On any curve or hill where the driver cannot see at least 500 feet ahead;

questions.question: What does a double-solid yellow line mean for passing?
choices: You may pass if the road ahead looks clear
Passing is always unsafe and usually illegal
You may pass only if the vehicle ahead is turning left
You may pass if you can see 500 feet ahead
questions.explanation: Places where passing is always unsafe and usually illegal include wherever there is a double-solid yellow line.
questions.sourceQuote: Wherever there is a double-solid yellow line;

questions.question: Passing on the right is against the law except in which situation?
choices: On highways having at least two lanes traveling in each direction
When the vehicle ahead is driving below the posted speed limit
When the road is clear and you are in a hurry
When the driver ahead waves you around
questions.explanation: Passing on the right is against the law except in areas where it is specifically permitted, such as on highways having at least two lanes traveling in each direction.
questions.sourceQuote: On highways having at least two lanes traveling in each direction;

questions.question: On a three-lane highway, when may you pass?
choices: In any lane if the road is clear
Only in the center lane and only where it is marked for passing in your direction
questions.explanation: On three-lane highways you must not pass except in the center lane, and then only where the center lane is marked for passing in your direction.
questions.sourceQuote: you must not pass except in the center lane, and then only where the center lane is marked for passing in your direction.

questions.question: You are being passed and the driver of the passing vehicle blows the horn. What must you do?
choices: Speed up to keep pace with the passing vehicle
Move to the left side of your lane
Sound your horn to warn the other driver
Move to the right edge of the road
questions.explanation: When you are being passed, you must help the other driver pass. If the driver blows the horn, move to the right edge of the road and never increase your speed.
questions.sourceQuote: If the driver of the passing vehicle blows the horn, move to the right edge of the road.

questions.question: You blow your horn to signal the driver ahead that you intend to pass. What does that horn signal do?
choices: It places the driver of the vehicle you are passing under a legal obligation to help you pass
It gives you the right to pass even in a no-passing zone
It requires the driver ahead to stop
questions.explanation: The horn signal places the driver of the vehicle you are passing under a legal obligation to help you pass.
questions.sourceQuote: The horn signal places the driver of the vehicle you are passing under a legal obligation to help you pass.

questions.question: Under what condition have you NOT passed safely?
choices: If you use your turn signal during the pass
If you pass at least two feet to the left
If the vehicle you have passed must slow down to allow you back into your correct lane
questions.explanation: You have not passed safely if the vehicle you have passed must slow down to allow you back into your correct lane.
questions.sourceQuote: You have not passed safely if the vehicle you have passed must slow down to allow you back into your correct lane.

questions.question: When backing your vehicle, how should you steer and look?
choices: Steer with your right hand and look over your left shoulder
Steer with your left hand and look over your right shoulder through the back window
Steer with both hands and rely on your mirrors
Steer with your left hand and look through the side window
questions.explanation: To maintain a full view of what is behind the vehicle, steer with your left hand and look over your right shoulder through the back window. Do not depend on mirrors alone or looking through the side window.
questions.sourceQuote: steer with your left hand and look over your right shoulder through the back window

questions.question: How far in advance must you signal before turning or stopping?
questions.explanation: Signal at least the last 100 feet before turning or stopping. If the speed limit is 45 mph or more, signal at least the last 200 feet before turning.
questions.sourceQuote: Signal at least the last 100 feet before turning or stopping.

questions.question: The posted speed limit is 50 mph. How far in advance must you signal before turning?
questions.explanation: If the speed limit is 45 mph or more, signal at least the last 200 feet before turning. The faster you are driving, the farther ahead you should signal.
questions.sourceQuote: If the speed limit is 45 mph or more, signal at least the last 200 feet before turning.

questions.question: Which hand signal means you are turning right?
choices: Arm and hand straight out, pointing the first finger
Arm straight out with the forearm and hand straight up, palm facing forward
Arm and hand pointing down, palm facing back
questions.explanation: Hand signals are given from the driver's window using the left arm and hand. To signal a right turn, hold the arm straight out and the forearm and hand straight up, palm facing forward.
questions.sourceQuote: To signal a right turn, hold the arm straight out and the forearm and hand straight up, palm facing forward.

questions.question: When you must stop at a railroad grade crossing, where must you stop?
choices: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
Within 15 feet but not less than 5 feet from the nearest rail
At least 100 feet from the nearest rail
questions.explanation: The driver shall stop within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad and shall not proceed until it can be done safely.
questions.sourceQuote: shall stop within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad

questions.question: When may you stop on railroad tracks?
choices: When traffic ahead is backed up
When you are waiting for a gate to rise
Never stop on train tracks for any reason
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing sign means you must approach with caution, prepare to stop and never stop on train tracks for any reason.
questions.sourceQuote: Never stop on train tracks for any reason

questions.question: You are crossing the tracks when the warning lights begin flashing and the gates start to come down. What should you do?
choices: Stop and back up off the tracks
Stop before the gate and wait
Sound your horn and continue slowly
Do not stop and do not back up; keep moving
questions.explanation: If you are crossing the tracks and the warning lights begin flashing or gates start to come down, do not stop, do not backup, keep moving. If you stop and try to back up, your vehicle may stall.
questions.sourceQuote: do not stop, do not backup, KEEP MOVING

questions.question: How should you enter an interstate highway?
choices: Use the acceleration lane until your speed matches other traffic, then merge safely
Stop at the end of the entrance ramp and wait for a gap
Merge at a slow speed so other drivers can see you
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate, use the acceleration lane until your vehicle's speed matches that of the other traffic and then merge safely.
questions.sourceQuote: When entering the interstate, use the acceleration lane until your vehicle’s speed matches that of the other traffic and then merge safely;

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?
choices: Back up along the shoulder to the exit
Stop and wait for traffic to clear, then turn around
Signal other drivers and make a U-turn at the next median opening
Proceed to the next exit and leave the highway there
questions.explanation: If you miss an exit, do not slow down, back up or try to turn around. Proceed to the next exit and leave the highway there instead.
questions.sourceQuote: If you miss an exit, do not slow down, back up or try to turn around. Proceed to the next exit and leave the highway there instead.

questions.question: When you are moving straight ahead through an intersection, what must you never do?
questions.explanation: Never change lanes while you are moving straight ahead through an intersection.
questions.sourceQuote: Never change lanes while you are moving straight ahead through an intersection.

questions.question: At an intersection without traffic signs or signals, which vehicle has the right of way?
choices: The vehicle already in the intersection
The vehicle that is traveling faster
The vehicle that is closer to the intersection
questions.explanation: In intersections without traffic signs or signals, the vehicle already in the intersection has the right of way ahead of any vehicle that has not yet entered.
questions.sourceQuote: The vehicle already in the intersection has the right of way

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an intersection without signs or signals at the same time. Which one has the right of way?
questions.explanation: When two or more vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the vehicle to the right has the right of way.
questions.sourceQuote: the vehicle to the right has the right of way;

questions.question: Two vehicles face each other at an intersection. One is going straight and the other wants to turn left. Who has the right of way?
choices: The driver turning left, if they signal first
Whichever driver enters the intersection first
questions.explanation: If one driver is going straight while the other wants to turn left, the driver who wants to turn must wait. The driver who is traveling straight ahead has the right of way.
questions.sourceQuote: If one driver is going straight while the other wants to turn left, the driver who wants to turn must wait.

questions.question: At intersections without traffic signals, when do pedestrians have the right of way?
choices: Only when they are wearing light-colored clothing
Only when a crossing guard is present
Only in crosswalks marked with white lines
When they are in marked crosswalks or in unmarked crosswalks formed by imaginary lines extending from the sidewalks
questions.explanation: At intersections without traffic signals, pedestrians have the right of way if they are in marked crosswalks or in unmarked crosswalks formed by imaginary lines extending from the sidewalks across the streets.
questions.sourceQuote: pedestrians have the right of way if they are in marked crosswalks or in unmarked crosswalks

questions.question: Pedestrians are crossing with a green signal. Who has the right of way?
choices: The pedestrians, over all vehicles including those turning across their path
Whichever arrives at the crosswalk first
questions.explanation: When crossing with a green signal, pedestrians have the right of way over all vehicles, including those turning across the paths of the pedestrians.
questions.sourceQuote: When crossing with a green signal, pedestrians have the right of way over all vehicles,

questions.question: A pedestrian is still in the street when the traffic signal changes to red. What must drivers do?
choices: Allow the pedestrian to complete the crossing safely
Sound the horn so the pedestrian hurries
Proceed because the pedestrian is crossing against the signal
questions.explanation: If a traffic signal changes to yellow or red while any pedestrian remains in the street, drivers must allow the pedestrian to complete the crossing safely.
questions.sourceQuote: drivers must allow the pedestrian to complete the crossing safely.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a stop sign. What does the law require?
choices: Slow down and proceed if no traffic is visible
Stop only if another vehicle is approaching
Come to a complete stop and yield to traffic on the through-street
Stop, then proceed without yielding if you arrived first
questions.explanation: When you approach an intersection with a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop and yield to the traffic on the through-street. Do not move ahead or turn until you can proceed safely.
questions.sourceQuote: When you approach an intersection with a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop and yield to the traffic on the through-street.

questions.question: When you exit a private driveway, to whom must you yield?
choices: Only to vehicles on your side of the road
No one, if you signal first
questions.explanation: When exiting a private driveway, stop and yield to all other vehicles and pedestrians.
questions.sourceQuote: When exiting a private driveway, stop and yield to all other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: As you approach a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
choices: Any vehicle or bicyclist already in the roundabout
Vehicles approaching the roundabout from behind
questions.explanation: Drivers yield to any vehicles or bicyclists already in the roundabout. Those already in it do not yield to approaching vehicles.
questions.sourceQuote: Drivers yield to any vehicles or bicyclists already in the roundabout.

questions.question: In which direction does traffic move in a roundabout?
choices: In the direction marked for your lane
Toward the center of the roundabout
questions.explanation: Everyone using the roundabout moves in a counterclockwise direction.
questions.sourceQuote: Everyone using the roundabout moves in a counterclockwise direction

questions.question: Who has the right of way at a railroad crossing?
choices: The first vehicle to reach the crossing
Vehicles, if the crossing has no gates or lights
questions.explanation: The train always has the right of way. Trains have the right of way over all highway traffic.
questions.sourceQuote: The train always has the right of way

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in cities and towns in North Carolina?
questions.explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit is 35 mph in cities and towns. Special speed limits may be posted for special areas.
questions.sourceQuote: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit is 35 mph in cities and towns.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit outside cities and towns?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limits are 35 mph in cities and towns, 45 mph for school buses, 55 mph for school activity buses and outside cities and towns, and 70 mph on interstates.
questions.sourceQuote: Outside cities and towns 55

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on North Carolina interstates?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit for interstates is 70 mph.
questions.sourceQuote: For interstates 70

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, approximately how many feet does a vehicle traveling 55 mph need to stop completely?
questions.explanation: Even with ideal conditions, if you are traveling 55 miles per hour your vehicle requires approximately 211 feet to stop completely.
questions.sourceQuote: Even with ideal conditions, if you are traveling 55 miles per hour your vehicle requires approximately 211 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: What does the two-second rule mean?
choices: Wait two seconds at a stop sign before proceeding
Signal at least two seconds before changing lanes
Allow two seconds between the time the vehicle ahead of you passes a given point and the time your vehicle reaches the same point
questions.explanation: The two-second rule says you should allow two seconds between the time the vehicle ahead of you passes a given point and the time your vehicle reaches the same point. Following too closely is a leading cause of traffic crashes.
questions.sourceQuote: allow two seconds between the time the vehicle ahead of you passes a given point and the time your vehicle reaches the same point.

questions.question: Studies show that which vehicle is much more likely to cause or be involved in a crash?
choices: One moving at a speed considerably below the posted limit
One moving at a normal speed
One moving exactly at the posted speed limit
questions.explanation: Studies show that the vehicle moving at a speed considerably below the posted limit is much more likely to cause or be involved in a crash than the vehicle moving at a normal speed.
questions.sourceQuote: vehicle moving at a speed considerably below the posted limit is much more likely to cause or be involved in a crash

questions.question: When backing your vehicle, how fast should you go?
questions.explanation: Back very slowly, not more than 10 mph. Your vehicle is harder to control and to stop when it is backing.
questions.sourceQuote: Back very slowly, not more than 10 mph

questions.question: At what speeds does the modern roundabout require vehicles to travel?
questions.explanation: The modern roundabout is much smaller than older traffic circles and requires vehicles to travel at lower speeds of 15 to 20 mph, making them safer than traffic circles.
questions.sourceQuote: requires vehicles to travel at lower speeds (15–20 mph),

questions.question: If traffic is collecting behind you while you are driving, what is it wise to do?
choices: Speed up to keep traffic moving
Wave the other drivers around you
Pull over to the side of the road, stop and allow the vehicles to pass
Drive at exactly the posted speed limit
questions.explanation: If traffic is collecting behind you, it is wise to pull over to the side of the road, stop and allow the vehicles to pass.
questions.sourceQuote: If traffic is collecting behind you, it is wise to pull over to the side of the road, stop and allow the vehicles to pass.

questions.question: Besides the posted limit, what speed must you never drive at?
choices: A speed that is unreasonable or unwise given the existing conditions
A speed lower than the flow of traffic
questions.explanation: Never drive faster than the posted speed limit or at a speed that is unreasonable or unwise given the existing conditions.
questions.sourceQuote: Never drive faster than the posted speed limit or at a speed that is unreasonable or unwise given the existing conditions.

questions.question: Why must you be able to see farther ahead when you are moving faster?
choices: So you can read road signs sooner
So you can save fuel on the highway
So you can change lanes more often
To allow enough distance for stopping
questions.explanation: The faster you are moving, the farther ahead you must be able to see to allow enough distance for stopping.
questions.sourceQuote: The faster you are moving, the farther ahead you must be able to see to allow enough distance for stopping.

questions.question: On which side of the road should you always park?
choices: The right side, except on one-way streets
Either side, as long as you are within 25 feet of the curb
questions.explanation: Always park on the right side of the road, except on one-way streets.
questions.sourceQuote: Always park on the right side of the road, except on one-way streets.

questions.question: Before pulling out from a parallel parking space, what should you do?
choices: Signal a right turn and move slowly
Sound your horn and wait for other drivers to stop
Check for approaching traffic and give a left-turn signal
questions.explanation: Before pulling out from a parallel parking space, check for approaching traffic and give a left-turn signal, unless you are parked on the left side of a one-way street.
questions.sourceQuote: Before pulling out from a parallel parking space, check for approaching traffic and give a left-turn signal,

questions.question: How close to a fire hydrant may you park?
questions.explanation: You should not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or the entrance to a fire station.
questions.sourceQuote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or entrance to a fire station;

questions.question: How close to the curb line of an intersecting street may you park?
questions.explanation: Do not park within 25 feet of the curb line of an intersecting street, or within 15 feet of the intersecting right of way lines if there is no curb.
questions.sourceQuote: Within 25 feet of the curb line of an intersecting street or within 15 feet of the intersecting right of way lines if there is no curb;

questions.question: Which of these is not a legal place to park?
choices: On the right side of a one-way street
On a crosswalk, sidewalk or bridge
In a space marked for handicap use, with a placard
questions.explanation: You should not park on a crosswalk, sidewalk or bridge.
questions.sourceQuote: On a crosswalk, sidewalk or bridge;

questions.question: In front of which of the following must you not park?
choices: A marked parking space on the right side of a two-way street
questions.explanation: You should not park at an intersection or in front of a driveway.
questions.sourceQuote: At an intersection or in front of a driveway;

questions.question: Parking on the paved or primary-travel portion of a highway is illegal. When is parking on the shoulder also against the law?
choices: Whenever the speed limit is above 45 mph
Unless the parked vehicle can be seen by approaching drivers from both directions for at least 200 feet
Whenever the road has no shoulder
Whenever the vehicle is left unattended
questions.explanation: Parking on the shoulder is against the law unless the parked vehicle can be seen by approaching drivers from both directions for a distance of at least 200 feet.
questions.sourceQuote: unless the parked vehicle can be seen by approaching drivers from both directions for a distance of at least 200 feet;

questions.question: When may you park in a space designated for handicap or disabled use?
choices: When you are only stopping for a few minutes
When no other spaces are available
When a passenger remains in the vehicle
Only when your vehicle displays a handicap license plate or a disability parking placard
questions.explanation: Do not park in spaces designated for handicap/disabled use unless your vehicle is displaying a handicap license plate or a disability parking placard.
questions.sourceQuote: unless your vehicle is displaying a handicap license plate or a disability parking placard.

questions.question: At 55 mph, about how long does it take a vehicle to travel the length of a football field?
questions.explanation: At 55 mph a vehicle covers the length of a football field in only 3.7 seconds, so there is no time for even a brief snooze.
questions.sourceQuote: At 55 mph, a vehicle travels the length of a football field in 3.7 seconds

questions.question: Which of these is a warning sign that you may be driving drowsy?
choices: You feel fully rested and alert
You remember the last several miles of your trip
You find it easy to keep your eyes open
You cannot remember the last few miles driven
questions.explanation: Not being able to remember the last few miles driven is listed as a warning sign of drowsy driving.
questions.sourceQuote: You cannot remember the last few miles driven.

questions.question: A driver under age 18 may use a cell phone while the vehicle is in motion only to:
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone or related technology while the vehicle is in motion, except to call 911 in an emergency.
questions.sourceQuote: Exceptions: calling 911 in an emergency

questions.question: Before taking any medication and driving, you should:
choices: Take a double dose to be safe
Find out how it will affect you
questions.explanation: The handbook says before you take any medication, find out how it will affect you, and do as little driving as possible while taking it.
questions.sourceQuote: Before you take any medication, find out how it will affect you.

questions.question: What is the only thing that sobers up a drinker?
questions.explanation: Coffee, a big meal and cold showers do not work; the only thing that sobers up a drinker is time.
questions.sourceQuote: The only thing that sobers up a drinker is time. Coffee, a big meal or cold showers will not work.

questions.question: Which statement describes how alcohol affects your driving?
choices: It improves your judgment on short trips
It reduces your ability to judge how fast you are moving and your distance from others
It has no effect on your sense of balance
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that reduces your ability to judge speed and distance and slows your reactions.
questions.sourceQuote: Reduces your ability to judge how fast you are moving or your distance from other cars, people or objects.

questions.question: When must the driver and all passengers wear a properly fastened seat belt?
choices: Only when traveling faster than 45 mph
At all times when the vehicle is in forward motion on a street or highway
questions.explanation: The seat belt law applies at all times when the vehicle is in forward motion on a street or highway in this state.
questions.sourceQuote: shall have a seat belt properly fastened about their body at all times when the vehicle is in forward motion on a street or highway

questions.question: If your vehicle is equipped with air bags, who must wear a seat belt?
choices: All occupants, even if the vehicle has air bags
No one, because air bags are enough
questions.explanation: Under the seat belt law, all occupants must wear seat belts even if the vehicle is equipped with air bags.
questions.sourceQuote: Under the seat belt law, all occupants MUST wear seat belts even if the vehicle is equipped with air bags.

questions.question: A child under age 8 who weighs less than 80 pounds must be secured in:
choices: A weight appropriate child passenger restraint system
No restraint if the child sits in the back seat
questions.explanation: A child under age 8 who weighs less than 80 pounds must be properly secured in a weight appropriate child passenger restraint system.
questions.sourceQuote: A child under age 8 and weighing less than 80 pounds must be properly secured in a weight appropriate child passenger restraint system.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an active passenger-side front air bag and a rear seat, a child under age 5 and under 40 pounds must:
choices: Ride in the front seat if the air bag is turned off
Ride on an adult lap in the front seat
Ride in the front seat with a lap belt
Ride properly secured in the rear seat
questions.explanation: Such a child must ride in the rear seat unless the child restraint system is designed for use with a front air bag system.
questions.sourceQuote: a child under age 5 and weighing less than 40 pounds must be properly secured in the rear seat

questions.question: Infants in rear-facing child safety seats should never:
choices: Be buckled in with a lap belt
Ride in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger-side air bag
questions.explanation: Infants in rear-facing seats should never ride in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger-side air bag.
questions.sourceQuote: Infants in rear-facing child safety seats should NEVER ride in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger-side air bag.

questions.question: North Carolina law prohibits children of what age from riding in the open bed of a pick-up truck?
questions.explanation: North Carolina law prohibits children less than age 16 from riding in the open bed of a pick-up truck.
questions.sourceQuote: North Carolina law prohibits children less than age 16 from riding in the open bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.question: You must make an immediate report of a crash to law enforcement when:
choices: Only when someone is taken to a hospital
Any person is killed or injured, or total damage is $1,000 or more
Only when a vehicle must be towed
questions.explanation: A report is required when anyone is killed or injured or when the total damage appears to amount to $1,000 or more.
questions.sourceQuote: any crash when any person is killed or injured or the total damage to vehicles and other property appears to amount to $1,000 or more

questions.question: What is the first thing you must do if you are involved in a crash?
choices: Drive to the nearest police station
Move the other vehicle off the road first
questions.explanation: You must stop the vehicle immediately; not stopping is a violation of the law.
questions.sourceQuote: You must stop the vehicle immediately.

questions.question: After a crash on a main lane with no injuries or fatalities, each vehicle should:
choices: Stay in the travel lane until an officer arrives
Be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder if it can be driven safely
Be left in place for the insurance company
Be pushed to the nearest intersection
questions.explanation: If there are no injuries or fatalities, each vehicle should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder when it can be driven safely under its own power.
questions.sourceQuote: each vehicle should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder of the road provided it can be driven safely under its own power

questions.question: Failure to make a required crash report may result in:
choices: A $10 fine and no other penalty
Nothing, if the crash was minor
Prosecution, and your driver license could be suspended
questions.explanation: Failure to make the report may result in prosecution, and your driver license could be suspended.
questions.sourceQuote: Failure to make the report may result in prosecution, and your driver license could be suspended.

questions.question: How far ahead should good drivers try to see on the roadway?
questions.explanation: Good drivers try to see 10 to 15 seconds ahead, about one city block.
questions.sourceQuote: Good drivers try to see 10 to 15 seconds ahead on the roadway (about one city block).

questions.question: Before changing lanes or turning, you should:
choices: Sound your horn and move over
Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot
Speed up to get ahead of traffic
questions.explanation: Mirrors leave blind spots, so look over your shoulder before any lane change or turn.
questions.sourceQuote: before you make any lane changes or turns, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder to see what is in the blind spot.

questions.question: When does the law require you to use headlights?
choices: Only on interstates and major highways
From sunset to sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less
questions.explanation: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is 400 feet or less.
questions.sourceQuote: The law requires use of headlights from sunset to sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less.

questions.question: An approaching driver is required to dim high-beam headlights. If the driver does not, you can remind the driver by:
choices: Sounding a long blast of your horn
questions.explanation: Blink your high beams once to remind the driver to dim; if the driver still does not dim, keep your lights on low beam.
questions.sourceQuote: you can remind the driver by blinking your high beams once

questions.question: On wet pavement you should allow yourself at least:
choices: Three times the normal following distance
questions.explanation: Stopping distances on wet pavement can increase from two to 10 times farther, so allow at least twice the normal following distance.
questions.sourceQuote: slow down and allow yourself at least twice the normal following distance.

questions.question: When should you never use cruise control?
choices: When it is raining or after it has been raining
questions.explanation: Cruise control delays your reaction if you start to hydroplane, so never use it in or after rain.
questions.sourceQuote: Never use cruise control when it is raining or after it has been raining.

questions.question: According to the handbook, on an icy road you should:
choices: Speed up to cross the ice quickly
questions.explanation: The handbook recommends reducing speed by more than half for packed snow and slowing to a crawl on ice.
questions.sourceQuote: It is recommended that you reduce speed by more than half for packed snow and slow to a crawl on ice.

questions.question: You must turn on your headlights in North Carolina:
choices: Whenever you are using your windshield wipers due to inclement weather
questions.explanation: All North Carolina motorists must use headlights whenever they use windshield wipers due to inclement weather.
questions.sourceQuote: All North Carolina motorists are required to use headlights whenever they are using windshield wipers due to inclement weather.

questions.question: If fog makes it impossible to see and you pull off the roadway, you should:
choices: Leave the vehicle from the driver side onto the road
Stand behind the vehicle to warn traffic
Keep driving slowly until the fog lifts
Leave the vehicle from the passenger side and stay away from the road
questions.explanation: In fog, pull far off the roadway, stop, turn on the emergency flashers, leave from the passenger side and stay away from the road.
questions.sourceQuote: Leave the vehicle from the passenger side and stay away from the road.

questions.question: What color signs identify a work zone?
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black letters are reserved strictly to identify work zones.
questions.sourceQuote: The orange signs with messages in black letters are reserved strictly to identify work zones.

questions.question: What can six inches of fast moving water do to a car?
questions.explanation: Six inches of fast moving water can sweep a car off the highway, and 12 inches can float it or turn it over.
questions.sourceQuote: six inches of fast moving water can sweep a car off the highway

questions.question: When a school bus displays its mechanical stop signal or flashing red lights, the driver of any other vehicle approaching must:
choices: Slow down and pass with caution
Stop only if children are visible
Pass if the bus is stopped in a driveway
Stop and not attempt to pass until the signal is withdrawn, the lights are off and the bus has started to move
questions.explanation: Traffic must stop and not attempt to pass a school bus until the mechanical stop signal is withdrawn, the red lights are turned off and the bus has started to move.
questions.sourceQuote: the driver of any other vehicle approaching the school bus must stop and not attempt to pass the school bus

questions.question: On a two-lane roadway, when a school bus stops for passengers:
choices: Only traffic behind the bus must stop
Only traffic in the bus lane must stop
No traffic must stop on two-lane roads
All traffic from both directions must stop
questions.explanation: On a two-lane roadway, all traffic from both directions must stop when a school bus stops for passengers.
questions.sourceQuote: Two-lane roadway: When school bus stops for passengers, all traffic from both directions must stop.

questions.question: On a divided highway of four lanes or more with a median separation, when a school bus stops for passengers:
choices: All traffic from both directions must stop
Only traffic in the center turning lane must stop
Only traffic in the opposite direction must stop
Only traffic following the bus must stop
questions.explanation: On a divided highway of four lanes or more with a median separation, only traffic following the bus must stop.
questions.sourceQuote: Divided highway of four lanes or more with a median separation: When school bus stops for passengers

questions.question: Why must drivers be careful around school bus stops even when no bus is in sight?
choices: Children must cross only at marked crosswalks
A police officer always directs traffic there
Children at a bus stop sometimes run into the street unexpectedly
Buses always stop in the travel lane
questions.explanation: Children waiting for the bus or leaving the bus might dart out into traffic, and children at a bus stop sometimes run into the street unexpectedly.
questions.sourceQuote: children at a bus stop sometimes will run into the street unexpectedly

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and a siren approaches from ahead or behind, you must:
choices: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop in your lane wherever you are
Drive to the right-hand curb or edge of the road and stop completely
Pull to the left and continue slowly
questions.explanation: Drive to the right-hand curb or edge of the road and stop completely until the emergency vehicle has passed.
questions.sourceQuote: drive to the right-hand curb or edge of the road and stop completely

questions.question: You must not park within how many feet of an emergency vehicle that has stopped to investigate a crash or give assistance?
questions.explanation: Do not park within 100 feet of an emergency vehicle that has stopped to investigate an accident or to give assistance.
questions.sourceQuote: Do not park within 100 feet of an emergency vehicle that has stopped to investigate an accident or to give assistance

questions.question: On a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median, do vehicles traveling in the opposite direction have to yield to an approaching emergency vehicle?
choices: Yes, all vehicles must always yield
No, that part of the law does not apply to them
questions.explanation: All vehicles must yield to an approaching emergency vehicle, except vehicles traveling the opposite direction on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median.
questions.sourceQuote: does not apply to vehicles traveling in the opposite direction of the emergency vehicle(s)

questions.question: On a highway with at least two lanes of traffic in the same direction, the Move Over law requires you to:
choices: Stop completely until the vehicle leaves
Reduce speed by exactly 10 mph and stay in your lane
Change lanes only if an officer directs you to
Move into a lane that is not the lane nearest the stopped emergency or service vehicle
questions.explanation: On such a highway you must move into a lane that is not nearest the parked or standing emergency vehicle and stay there until safely clear.
questions.sourceQuote: that is not the lane nearest the parked or standing emergency vehicle

questions.question: When you see emergency lights or hear a siren behind you, you should:
choices: Speed up to reach the next exit
Pull to the left edge of the road
Activate your turn signal and pull to the right, off the travel portion of the highway, at the nearest safe point
questions.explanation: Stay calm, activate your turn signal, pull to the right and off the travel portion of the highway at the nearest point where it is safe.
questions.sourceQuote: pull the vehicle always to the right, and off the travel portion of the highway at the nearest point where it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If there is no obvious safe place to stop when an officer is stopping you, you should turn on your four-way flashers and:
choices: Stop in the middle of the road
Continue at the same speed until the officer uses a loudspeaker
Reduce your speed by about 10 mph until you reach a safe place to stop
questions.explanation: With the four-way flashers on, reduce your speed by about 10 mph to show the officer you are aware, and stop at the nearest safe area.
questions.sourceQuote: turn on your emergency 4 way flashers and reduce your speed (by about 10 mph)

questions.question: If an unmarked car is stopping you and you are not sure it is a real law enforcement officer, you may:
choices: Drive home and ignore the stop
Speed up to reach a police station
Call 9-1-1 before pulling over to verify that an officer is conducting the stop
questions.explanation: If you have a legitimate concern about an unmarked car, you may call 9-1-1 before pulling over to verify the traffic stop.
questions.sourceQuote: you may call 9-1-1 before pulling over

questions.question: During a traffic stop, you are required to:
choices: Answer every question the officer asks
Exit the vehicle and walk back to the patrol car
Sign a statement admitting the violation
Identify yourself and provide your driver license and registration
questions.explanation: State law requires you to identify yourself and provide your driver license and registration; after that you may choose whether to answer additional questions.
questions.sourceQuote: you are required to identify yourself and provide your drivers license and registration for the vehicle

questions.question: During a traffic stop, you should not remove your seat belt unless:
choices: You are parked in a parking lot
The stop lasts more than five minutes
The officer asks you to do so
questions.explanation: You and all passengers should remain seated, and you should not remove your seat belt unless asked to do so by the officer.
questions.sourceQuote: Do not remove your seatbelt unless asked to do so by the officer.

questions.question: What types of crashes most typically involve farm equipment?
questions.explanation: Typical crashes with farm equipment include sideswipes and angle crashes, often while equipment turns left and a vehicle attempts to pass.
questions.sourceQuote: Typical crashes with farm equipment include sideswipes and angle crashes.

questions.question: Farm equipment on the road is required to have:
choices: One front white light and a rear red light visible for up to 500 feet
A flashing blue light on top
questions.explanation: Farm equipment must have one front white light and a rear red light visible up to 500 feet; two red reflectors at least four inches in diameter can replace the rear red light.
questions.sourceQuote: Farm equipment is required to have one front white light as well as a rear red light that is visible for up to 500 feet.

questions.question: Where is farm equipment legally entitled to travel in North Carolina?
choices: On most roads, but not on interstates
questions.explanation: Farm equipment is legally entitled to travel on most roads in North Carolina, except interstates.
questions.sourceQuote: Farm equipment is legally entitled to travel on most roads in North Carolina, except interstates.

questions.question: The key to safety when sharing the road with farm equipment is:
choices: Honk so the operator speeds up
Be patient, and let the operator move off the road at the nearest practical location so traffic can pass
Pass at the first opening in oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: Be patient; if farm equipment is delaying traffic, the operator should move off the road at the nearest practical location and let traffic pass.
questions.sourceQuote: the operator should move off the road at the nearest practical location and allow the traffic to pass.

questions.question: Every vehicle in a funeral procession must:
choices: Display a flag on the antenna
Use high-beam headlights at all times
Have its headlights on, and its hazard warning signals on if so equipped
questions.explanation: Every vehicle in a funeral procession must have its headlights on, and the hazard warning signals must also be on, if so equipped.
questions.sourceQuote: Every vehicle in a funeral procession must have its headlights on, and the hazard warning signals must also be on, if so equipped.

questions.question: After the lead vehicle of a funeral procession has crossed an intersection in accordance with the traffic signal:
choices: Each vehicle must stop again at the signal
The procession must stop and wait for a police escort
Only the last vehicle must stop
The other vehicles in the procession may proceed through the intersection without stopping
questions.explanation: Once the lead vehicle has crossed in accordance with the signal or has been directed through, all vehicles in the procession may proceed without stopping, using extra care.
questions.sourceQuote: all vehicles in the funeral procession may proceed through the intersection without stopping

questions.question: A driver must not knowingly:
choices: Drive between the vehicles in a funeral procession
questions.explanation: The driver of a vehicle must not knowingly drive between vehicles in a funeral procession.
questions.sourceQuote: The driver of a vehicle shall not knowingly drive between vehicles in a funeral procession.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while you are driving, you should:
choices: Shift into a lower gear and apply the emergency brake
questions.explanation: With brake failure, shift into a lower gear and apply the emergency brake; with an automatic transmission, apply the emergency brake and move the gear lever into low range.
questions.sourceQuote: Shift into a lower gear, release the clutch pedal (for manual transmissions) and apply the emergency brake.

questions.question: If your gas pedal sticks, you should:
choices: Turn the ignition off and coast
Shift to neutral and apply firm pressure to the brakes without locking the wheels
questions.explanation: Tap the gas pedal to try to unstick it, shift to neutral and apply firm pressure to the brakes without locking the wheels, then move completely off the road.
