questions.sourceQuote: Shift to neutral and apply firm pressure to the brakes without locking the wheels

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:
choices: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight, then reduce speed by lifting your foot from the accelerator and move completely off the road.
questions.sourceQuote: Hold the steering wheel tightly and try to keep the vehicle straight on your side of the road

questions.question: While you change a flat tire, your passengers should:
choices: Stay in the vehicle with seat belts fastened
Stand behind the vehicle to warn traffic
Stand in front of the vehicle to watch for traffic
Leave the vehicle by the passenger side and move off the road or shoulder
questions.explanation: Never allow passengers to remain in the vehicle during a tire change; they should leave by the passenger side and stay off the road and away from the front or rear of the vehicle.
questions.sourceQuote: Never allow passengers to remain in the vehicle during a tire change.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down and you need help, you should:
choices: Stand behind the vehicle and wave
Remain in the driver seat with the windows up
Walk along the road to look for help
Tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood
questions.explanation: Tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood; if it is dark, turn on the parking lights or emergency flashers.
questions.sourceQuote: tie a white cloth to the left door handle or the radio aerial and raise the hood of the vehicle

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, you should:
choices: Take your foot off the gas pedal and keep the steering wheel straight
Turn the steering wheel sharply to find grip
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas pedal, resist the instinct to brake, keep the steering wheel straight and let the vehicle slow until the tires grip again.
questions.sourceQuote: take your foot off the gas pedal. Resist your instinct to use the brakes. Keep your steering wheel straight

questions.question: If you find yourself in a skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
choices: In the opposite direction of the skid
Straight ahead and hold it there
In the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding
Toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: Ease off the accelerator and turn the steering wheel in the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding, then turn it back as the path straightens so you do not over-steer.
questions.sourceQuote: Turn the steering wheel in the direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding

questions.question: If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes and you must stop quickly, you should:
choices: Apply firm, steady pressure to the brake pedal and do not pump the brakes
questions.explanation: With ABS, brake hard and keep firm, steady pressure; pumping the pedal or releasing pressure reduces the effectiveness of the ABS.
questions.sourceQuote: Engage your anti-lock braking system using firm, steady pressure on the brake pedal. Do not PUMP anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: If an approaching vehicle crosses the center line into your path, you should:
choices: Swerve left into the oncoming lane
Stop in your lane and wait
Reduce speed, sound your horn and keep to the right even if it means running off the road
questions.explanation: Reduce speed immediately, sound your horn and keep to the right even if this means running off the road.
questions.sourceQuote: Keep to the right even if this means running off the road.

questions.question: If your vehicle runs off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:
choices: Brake hard and turn back onto the road
Brake and stop as fast as possible
Slowly remove your foot from the accelerator and steer straight ahead
Turn sharply back onto the pavement
questions.explanation: Do not immediately brake or try to turn back; ease off the accelerator, steer straight, let the engine slow the vehicle, then ease back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.sourceQuote: Do not immediately apply the brakes or try to turn back; you could skid, lose control or overturn

questions.question: You see this sign at an intersection. What does the law require you to do?
choices: Slow down and continue if the way looks clear
Come to a full stop and do not move again until you are sure the way is clear
Stop only when other traffic is present
Stop and then go without yielding to pedestrians
questions.explanation: The octagonal red STOP sign requires a full stop. You may not move again until you are sure the way is clear.
questions.sourceQuote: When you approach this sign, the law requires you to come to a FULL stop. Do not proceed to move again until you are sure the way is clear.
questions.imageAlt: Red octagonal STOP sign

questions.question: What must you do when you come to this sign?
choices: Stop completely and wait for a signal to change
Speed up to merge with traffic
Slow down and yield the right of way, stopping if needed
Continue at the same speed because other traffic must yield to you
questions.explanation: The yield sign is triangular with the point at the bottom. Slow down and yield the right of way; whether you must stop depends on the traffic on the intersecting street.
questions.sourceQuote: When you approach the yield sign, you must slow down and yield the right of way.
questions.imageAlt: Red and white triangular YIELD sign

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: Do not enter; you may not drive onto that road or lane
No parking is allowed on this street
questions.explanation: The DO NOT ENTER sign means you must not drive onto the road or lane it faces.
questions.sourceQuote: Failure to obey these signs is unsafe as well as a violation of the traffic laws.
questions.imageAlt: Square sign reading DO NOT ENTER

questions.question: You are about to enter a street and see this sign. What should you do?
choices: Move to the left lane and continue
Turn around, because you are facing oncoming traffic and going the wrong way
questions.explanation: The WRONG WAY sign warns that you are heading into opposing traffic. Turn around and get back into the correct direction.
questions.sourceQuote: Failure to obey these signs is unsafe as well as a violation of the traffic laws.
questions.imageAlt: Red and white rectangular WRONG WAY sign

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?
choices: The minimum speed you must drive
A speed that is only suggested for bad weather
The maximum legal speed on this road
The speed limit for trucks only
questions.explanation: The white rectangular SPEED LIMIT sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road.
questions.sourceQuote: Rectangular and square-shaped signs, which are normally black and white or red and white, are also used to show speed limits
questions.imageAlt: White rectangular SPEED LIMIT sign

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: Right turns are allowed only on a green light
Right turns are not allowed at this location
Right turns are permitted after a full stop
You must turn right at this intersection
questions.explanation: The red circle and slash over a right-turn arrow means right turns are prohibited.
questions.sourceQuote: Failure to obey these signs is unsafe as well as a violation of the traffic laws.
questions.imageAlt: White sign with a red circle and slash over a right-turn arrow

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?
choices: You must turn left at this intersection
Left turns are allowed only for buses
Left turns are not allowed at this location
There is a left-turn lane ahead
questions.explanation: The red circle and slash over a left-turn arrow means left turns are prohibited.
questions.sourceQuote: Failure to obey these signs is unsafe as well as a violation of the traffic laws.
questions.imageAlt: White sign with a red circle and slash over a left-turn arrow

questions.question: This sign means that you must not do which of the following?
choices: Turn around and go back the way you came
Make a right turn at the next corner
questions.explanation: The NO U-TURN sign prohibits U-turns at this location.
questions.sourceQuote: These signs will also have messages such as “NO U-TURN” or “KEEP RIGHT EXCEPT TO PASS.”
questions.imageAlt: White rectangular NO U-TURN sign

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: Do not drive in the left lane
Passing is allowed only at night
Do not stop on the road
Do not pass other vehicles on this section of road
questions.explanation: The DO NOT PASS sign marks the beginning of a no-passing zone, where a solid yellow line runs in your lane.
questions.sourceQuote: The pennant–shaped yellow warning sign emphasizes, rather than replaces, the rectangular regulatory “DO NOT PASS” sign.
questions.imageAlt: White rectangular DO NOT PASS sign

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: Traffic on this road moves only in the direction of the arrow
The road curves to the left ahead
You may turn left but not right
questions.explanation: The ONE WAY sign shows that traffic on the road or in the lane flows only in the direction of the arrow, so you must not drive against it.
questions.sourceQuote: Failure to obey these signs is unsafe as well as a violation of the traffic laws.
questions.imageAlt: White sign reading ONE WAY with an arrow pointing left

questions.question: What does this sign instruct you to do?
choices: Turn right at the next intersection
The right lane is closed ahead
Keep to the right of a divider or other obstruction
questions.explanation: The KEEP RIGHT sign tells you to pass to the right of a divider, island or other obstruction.
questions.sourceQuote: These signs will also have messages such as “NO U-TURN” or “KEEP RIGHT EXCEPT TO PASS.”
questions.imageAlt: White sign with a black arrow curving to the right around a divider

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A sharp left turn onto a side road
A curve to the left ahead
A winding road for the next several miles
questions.explanation: The yellow diamond with a left-curving arrow warns of a curve ahead. Slow down and drive with extra care.
questions.sourceQuote: Diamond-shaped signs are also caution or warning signs.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign with an arrow curving to the left

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: A curve to the right ahead
questions.explanation: The sign warns of a curve to the right. Slow down and stay in your lane.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign with an arrow curving to the right

questions.question: What does this sign tell you about the road ahead?
choices: There is one curve, then the road is straight
The road narrows to one lane
A series of curves begins ahead
questions.explanation: The winding road sign warns of a series of curves ahead. Slow down and drive with extra care.
questions.sourceQuote: Diamond-shaped signs are also caution or warning signs.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a winding road

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
questions.explanation: The sign shows a crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic entering the highway from the side roads.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a crossroad intersection

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: You must stop at this sign
A stop sign is ahead, so prepare to stop
Stop only if pedestrians are crossing
questions.explanation: The STOP AHEAD sign is placed far ahead of a stop sign when your view of the stop sign is blocked by a curve or other objects.
questions.sourceQuote: One of the most important caution signs is the “STOP AHEAD” sign.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign reading STOP AHEAD

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?
choices: Yield only to vehicles on your left
You have the right of way ahead
The road ahead is a one-way street
questions.explanation: The sign warns that a yield sign is ahead, so slow down and be ready to yield the right of way.
questions.sourceQuote: When you approach the yield sign, you must slow down and yield the right of way.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign reading YIELD AHEAD

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A traffic officer is directing traffic
The traffic signal ahead is out of order
questions.explanation: The sign warns of a traffic signal ahead, so be ready to stop.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a traffic signal

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: The right lane ends in one mile
Traffic from the right will merge into your lane
questions.explanation: The merge sign warns that traffic from another lane or ramp will join the through lanes. Watch for vehicles entering and adjust your speed.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing traffic merging from the right

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: The road narrows but both lanes continue
A new lane is being added
The shoulder becomes a travel lane
A lane ends ahead, so traffic must merge
questions.explanation: The sign shows that the right lane ends ahead. Merge safely into the lane that continues.
questions.sourceQuote: Diamond-shaped signs are also caution or warning signs.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing the right lane ending

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: The road becomes a divided highway
There are two lanes in each direction
Traffic will be moving in both directions ahead
Passing is permitted on both sides
questions.explanation: The sign warns that two-way traffic is ahead, so keep to your lane and do not drive left of the center line.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing two-way traffic

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A steep hill or downgrade ahead
questions.explanation: The sign warns of a steep grade ahead. Reduce speed and keep control of your vehicle on the downgrade.
questions.sourceQuote: Diamond-shaped signs are also caution or warning signs.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a steep downgrade

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: The road may flood in heavy rain
The road is slippery when wet, so slow down in rain
A bridge may freeze in winter
questions.explanation: The sign warns that the road surface is slippery when it is wet. Slow down and allow extra space when the road is wet.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a car with skid marks

questions.question: You see this round yellow sign with a black cross and the letters RR. What does it mean?
choices: A railroad crossing is ahead, so slow down
A railroad maintenance yard is next to the highway
Trains may cross the highway only at night
The railroad crossing ahead is closed
questions.explanation: This circular sign gives advance warning of a railroad crossing. Slow down and stop if necessary to be sure you can safely clear the crossing.
questions.sourceQuote: A circular sign, with a black cross and the black letters “RR” on a yellow background, gives advance warning of a railroad crossing.
questions.imageAlt: Round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: A bicycle lane runs beside the road
Bicycles are not allowed on this road
questions.explanation: The sign warns that bicycles cross the road ahead. Watch for riders and be ready to slow down.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a bicycle

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
choices: Pedestrians are not allowed on this road
Pedestrians cross the road here, so be ready to stop
questions.explanation: The sign warns that pedestrians cross the road ahead. Slow down and be ready to yield to people in the crossing.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a walking pedestrian

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
choices: Hunting is allowed in this area
A zoo or wildlife park is ahead
Deer often cross the road here
Livestock will be on the road
questions.explanation: The sign warns that deer often cross the road in this area. Slow down and be ready for animals on the road.
questions.sourceQuote: When you see one of these signs, drive with extra care.
questions.imageAlt: Yellow diamond sign showing a leaping deer

questions.question: What does this yellow pennant-shaped sign mean?
choices: Passing is allowed on both sides
You are entering a no-passing zone
You must merge to the left
questions.explanation: The pennant points to the beginning of a no-passing zone, where a solid yellow line runs in your lane.
questions.sourceQuote: The pennant is located on the left side of the road and points to the beginning of the no-passing zone (solid yellow line in your lane).
questions.imageAlt: Yellow pennant sign reading NO PASSING ZONE

questions.question: What does this orange diamond-shaped sign mean?
choices: Construction or maintenance work is ahead
Traffic is being detoured for a special event
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs with black messages warn about construction or maintenance areas. Slow down and drive with extra care.
questions.sourceQuote: Diamond-shaped caution or warning signs that are orange with black messages warn about construction or maintenance areas.
questions.imageAlt: Orange diamond sign reading ROAD WORK 1000 FT

questions.question: You are at a railroad crossing and see this crossbuck sign. What does it mean?
choices: The railroad track has been abandoned
You must yield to trains at this crossing
Trains stop before crossing the road
The crossing is for pedestrians only
questions.explanation: The crossbuck marks the railroad crossing itself, with the words RAILROAD CROSSING in black on the white crosspieces. Yield to trains and check both directions before crossing.
questions.sourceQuote: The words “RAILROAD CROSSING” are printed in black on the white crosspieces.
questions.imageAlt: White X-shaped crossbuck sign reading RAILROAD CROSSING

questions.question: What does this five-sided sign mean?
choices: A school zone or school crossing is ahead
questions.explanation: The pentagon sign warns of a school zone or school crossing. Be especially watchful for children in these areas.
questions.sourceQuote: The five-sided (or pentagon) sign warns of a school zone or a school crossing.
questions.imageAlt: Fluorescent yellow-green pentagon sign showing two schoolchildren figures

questions.question: What does this sign assembly mean?
choices: Children are crossing the road here
The school bus stop is on the left
The school speed limit ends here
School parking is to the left
questions.explanation: The school sign with an arrow plaque marks a school crossing. Watch for children in the area.
questions.sourceQuote: You should be especially watchful for children in these areas.
questions.imageAlt: Fluorescent yellow-green pentagon sign with schoolchildren figures above a plaque with a left-pointing arrow

questions.question: What does this red, white and blue shield sign identify?
questions.explanation: Interstate highways are marked by a red, white and blue shield.
questions.sourceQuote: Interstate highways are marked by a red, white and blue shield.
questions.imageAlt: Red, white and blue interstate shield for I-40

questions.question: What kind of route is marked by this shield-shaped sign?
questions.explanation: Route markers for U.S. highways are in the shape of a shield.
questions.sourceQuote: Route markers for U.S. highways are in the shape of a shield.
questions.imageAlt: White shield-shaped U.S. route marker for US 64

questions.question: What does this diamond-shaped route marker identify?
questions.explanation: North Carolina route markers are diamond shaped.
questions.sourceQuote: North Carolina route markers are diamond shaped.
questions.imageAlt: Diamond-shaped North Carolina route marker for NC 24

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing whenever which of the following happens?
choices: A train passed through the crossing earlier in the day
A flagger, signal or gate indicates an approaching train
You see a crossbuck sign at the crossing
The crossing has more than one track
questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, signal or gate indicates an approaching train, and remain stopped until the gate lifts or the signal or flagger says it is safe to proceed.
questions.sourceQuote: You must stop at a railroad crossing whenever a flagger, signal or gate indicates an approaching train.

questions.question: What does the DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS sign remind a driver to do?
choices: Stop only if a train is visible
Stop before the tracks and wait for a green light
Do not drive across the tracks at night
Never stop on the railroad track for any reason
questions.explanation: The sign reminds drivers not to stop on the railroad track for any reason.
questions.sourceQuote: The DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS sign reminds the driver not to stop on the railroad track for any reason.

questions.question: A steady circular green traffic signal means that you may do which of the following?
choices: Proceed cautiously straight through or make a turn, yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when turning
Proceed only if no pedestrians are nearby
Turn only, because through traffic must wait
Proceed without checking for other traffic
questions.explanation: Green means you are permitted to proceed cautiously straight through or turn. Turning vehicles must yield the right of way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.sourceQuote: A circular green signal means you are permitted to proceed cautiously straight through or make a turn.

questions.question: The signal turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?
choices: Speed up to clear the intersection before the red
Stop, unless you are too close to the intersection to stop safely
Always continue through at the same speed
Stop in the middle of the intersection and wait
questions.explanation: Yellow means caution and shows that the signal is about to turn red. Stop unless you are too close to stop safely, and never speed up to beat the red.
questions.sourceQuote: Stop for a yellow signal unless you are too close to the intersection to stop safely

questions.question: You are stopped at a steady red circular signal and there is no NO TURN ON RED sign. When may you turn right?
choices: Only when the light turns green
At any time, because right turns are always allowed
After coming to a complete stop, if you yield to other traffic and pedestrians
Only if a police officer waves you through
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says NO TURN ON RED, a right turn can be made after coming to a complete stop. Right-turning vehicles must yield the right of way to other traffic and to pedestrians using the intersection.
questions.sourceQuote: Unless there is a sign indicating “NO TURN ON RED,” a right turn can be made after coming to a complete stop.

questions.question: What does a green arrow signal mean?
choices: You may make the movement only after yielding to all traffic
The signal is about to change to red
You must stop before making the movement
You have a protected movement and may cautiously enter the intersection to make the movement indicated
questions.explanation: A green arrow gives you a protected movement. You may cautiously enter the intersection to make the movement shown by the arrow.
questions.sourceQuote: A green arrow means that you have a “protected” movement and are permitted to cautiously enter the intersection

questions.question: A flashing yellow arrow signal for a turn means that which of the following is true?
choices: No turns are allowed in that direction
The turn is permitted, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
The turn is protected and you do not need to yield
The signal is not working and you should wait
questions.explanation: With a flashing yellow arrow, the turn is permitted but drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.sourceQuote: When the flashing yellow arrow is shown, the indicated turn is permitted but drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal has the same meaning as which of the following?
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: stop and do not move until you can enter the intersection without interfering with approaching traffic.
questions.sourceQuote: The flashing red signal has the same meaning as the stop sign

questions.question: You reach an intersection where the traffic light has failed because of a power outage, and no officer is directing traffic. What should you do?
choices: Proceed through without stopping, since the light is dark
Treat the intersection as if a stop sign controlled all approaches
Wait at the intersection until the light comes back on
Turn around and find another route
questions.explanation: When a traffic light has malfunctioned, approach the intersection and proceed as though a stop sign controls all approaches to it.
questions.sourceQuote: you should approach the intersection and proceed as though the intersection is controlled by a stop sign on all approaches

questions.question: You are on a freeway entrance ramp and the ramp meter signal ahead is dark. What should you do?
choices: Proceed without stopping and merge onto the freeway as conditions allow
Stop and wait for the signal to turn green
Back up and take another ramp
Stop and then go on the red
questions.explanation: When a ramp meter display is dark or not showing red or green, a vehicle may proceed without stopping and merge onto the freeway as normal conditions allow.
questions.sourceQuote: When the display is dark or not emitting a red or green display, a vehicle may proceed without stopping and enter the freeway

questions.question: A traffic officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the signals are working. Whose directions should you follow?
questions.explanation: Obey the officer's hand signals instead of the normal traffic signals or signs.
questions.sourceQuote: If so, obey the officer’s hand signals instead of the normal traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: What do yellow lines on the roadway separate?
choices: Travel lanes moving in opposite directions
Travel lanes moving in the same direction
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate travel lanes moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.
questions.sourceQuote: Yellow lines separate travel lanes moving in opposite directions. White lines separate travel lanes moving in the same direction.

questions.question: A two-lane, two-way road has a broken (skipped) yellow center line. What does this mean?
choices: Passing is not permitted in either direction
Passing with care is permitted in both directions
Passing is permitted only in the direction of the solid line
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line is the center line on a two-lane, two-way road where passing with care is permitted in both directions.
questions.sourceQuote: A yellow skipped or broken line is used as the center line on a two-lane, two-way road where passing with care is permitted

questions.question: What do continuous, double, solid yellow center lines mean?
choices: You may cross them to pass when the road is clear
Passing is allowed only at night
You cannot cross them to pass in either direction
The lanes travel in the same direction
questions.explanation: Continuous double solid yellow center lines may not be crossed to pass in either direction.
questions.sourceQuote: When continuous, double, solid, yellow lines are the center lines, you cannot cross them to pass in either direction.

questions.question: Single, solid white lines along the roadway are used as which of the following?
choices: Markings for the two-way left-turn lane
Right-edge lines that guide traffic traveling in the same direction
questions.explanation: Single, solid white lines are right-edge lines along the roadway and guide traffic traveling in the same direction.
questions.sourceQuote: Single, solid, white lines are used as right-edge lines along the roadway and for guiding traffic traveling in the same direction.

questions.question: On a divided highway, what does a single, solid yellow line on your left mark?
choices: The right edge of the roadway
The left edge of the roadway
The center of a two-way left-turn lane
A no-passing zone for the lane to your left
questions.explanation: Single, solid yellow lines are left-edge lines on divided highways. If you see the reverse, you are traveling in the wrong direction.
questions.sourceQuote: Single, solid, yellow lines are used as left-edge lines on divided highways.

questions.question: On some multi-lane highways a special center lane is reserved for two-way left-turn movements. What must you not use that lane for?
choices: Making a left turn from either direction
Entering a driveway on the left
Passing another vehicle or merging into traffic
questions.explanation: The two-way left-turn lane is reserved exclusively for two-way left-turn movements and must not be used for passing or merging.
questions.sourceQuote: The two-way left-turn lane must not be used for passing another vehicle or for the purpose of merging into traffic.

questions.question: What do blue reflective pavement markers on a roadway indicate?
choices: The edge of a bicycle lane
The location of nearby fire hydrants or water supplies for fire-fighting units
questions.explanation: Blue reflective pavement markers indicate the location of nearby fire hydrants or water supplies for fire-fighting units. Red markers indicate wrong-way movements.
questions.sourceQuote: blue reflective pavement markers on roadways indicate the location of nearby fire hydrants or water supplies for fire-fighting units

questions.question: A stop sign or traffic light requires you to stop. Where must you stop?
choices: Anywhere within 50 feet of the intersection
In the crosswalk so that other drivers can see you
One car length past the stop line
At the appropriately marked stop line, or if there is none, before entering the intersection where you have a view of the intersecting street
questions.explanation: A driver must stop at the appropriately marked stop line. If there is no stop line or marked crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection where you have a view of the intersecting street.
questions.sourceQuote: the driver must stop at the appropriately marked stop line

questions.question: Under North Carolina state law, bicycles are:
choices: vehicles that must obey traffic laws
questions.explanation: State law considers bicycles to be vehicles. Bicyclists must obey the same traffic laws as other drivers, including DWI laws.
questions.sourceQuote: Because bicycles are vehicles, bicyclists must obey the same traffic laws as other drivers, this includes DWI laws.

questions.question: Bicyclists may legally choose to ride:
choices: In bicycle lanes, on paved shoulders, or in all-purpose travel lanes
questions.explanation: Bicyclists may ride in bicycle lanes, on paved shoulders, or in all-purpose travel lanes, choosing based on roadway conditions and conflicts with right-turning traffic.
questions.sourceQuote: Bicyclists may choose to ride in bicycle lanes, on paved shoulders, or in all-purpose travel lanes.

questions.question: A driver may pass a bicyclist only when:
choices: The bicyclist waves the driver around
There is abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic in the opposing lane
The driver sounds the horn first
There is at least one foot of space
questions.explanation: Drivers wishing to pass a bicyclist may do so only when there is abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic in the opposing lane.
questions.sourceQuote: Drivers wishing to pass a bicyclist may do so only when there is abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic is in the opposing lane.

questions.question: The safest way to pass a bicyclist is to:
choices: Stay in your lane and slow down
Follow closely until the bicyclist pulls over
questions.explanation: The safest way to pass a bicyclist is to change lanes. To pass a cyclist lawfully, a driver must follow vehicle passing laws.
questions.sourceQuote: The safest way to pass a bicyclist is to change lanes.

questions.question: Bicyclists should ride:
choices: Against the flow of traffic to see oncoming cars
With the flow of traffic, not against it
In the center of the road at all times
questions.explanation: It is especially important for bicyclists to go with the flow of traffic. Motorists often do not look in the direction of bicyclists riding the wrong way.
questions.sourceQuote: It is especially important for bicyclists to go with the flow of traffic, NOT against the flow.

questions.question: At night, the law requires a bicycle to have a light on the front visible for a distance of at least:
questions.explanation: At night the law requires a light on the front visible for at least 300 feet and a red light or reflector on the rear visible for at least 200 feet.
questions.sourceQuote: the law requires that a bicycle be equipped with a light on the front visible for a distance of at least 300 feet

questions.question: At night, a bicycle must have a red light or reflector on the rear visible for a distance of at least:
questions.explanation: The rear of a bicycle must show a red light or reflector visible for at least 200 feet at night.
questions.sourceQuote: a red light or reflector on the rear visible for a distance of at least 200 feet

questions.question: Who must wear an approved protective bicycle helmet?
choices: All bicycle riders and passengers under age 16
questions.explanation: All bicycle riders and passengers under age 16 must wear an approved protective bicycle helmet and must be seated on a saddle seat.
questions.sourceQuote: All bicycle riders and passengers under age 16 must wear an approved protective bicycle helmet

questions.question: A bicycle passenger who weighs less than 40 pounds or is less than 40 inches tall must:
choices: Ride in front of the rider
Be seated in a bicycle restraining seat
questions.explanation: A passenger weighing less than 40 pounds or less than 40 inches in height must be seated in a bicycle restraining seat.
questions.sourceQuote: A passenger weighing less than 40 pounds or less than 40 inches in height must be seated in a bicycle restraining seat.

questions.question: When walking along a road, a pedestrian should:
choices: Walk on the right side with traffic
Walk on the left side of the road facing traffic
Walk in the center of the lane
Walk on the right shoulder facing away from traffic
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should always walk on the left side of the road facing traffic, and make themselves visible to drivers.
questions.sourceQuote: Walk on the left side of the road facing traffic

questions.question: At night, pedestrians should:
choices: Walk in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: At night it is more difficult for drivers to see pedestrians, so a pedestrian should use a flashlight.
questions.sourceQuote: At night, remember that it is more difficult for drivers to see you

questions.question: In cities, about how many of the persons killed by motor vehicle crashes are pedestrians?
questions.explanation: In cities, about two of every five persons killed by motor vehicle crashes are pedestrians.
questions.sourceQuote: In cities, about two of every five persons killed by motor vehicle crashes are pedestrians

questions.question: In rural areas, about how many of the persons killed by motor vehicle crashes are pedestrians?
questions.explanation: In rural areas, the rate is about one of every 10 persons killed by motor vehicle crashes.
questions.sourceQuote: in rural areas, the rate is about one of every 10

questions.question: Most pedestrians killed in motor vehicle crashes are:
choices: Children, elderly persons, or those who have been drinking alcoholic beverages
questions.explanation: Most of the pedestrians killed are children, elderly persons or those who have been drinking alcoholic beverages.
questions.sourceQuote: Most of the pedestrians killed are children, elderly persons or those who have been drinking alcoholic beverages.

questions.question: Compared with passenger cars, heavy trucks:
choices: Cannot gain speed as quickly, especially while traveling uphill
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks cannot gain speed as quickly as cars, especially while traveling uphill.
questions.sourceQuote: Heavy trucks cannot gain speed as quickly as cars, especially while traveling uphill.

questions.question: Because of its large size, a tractor-trailer often:
choices: Appears to be traveling at a slower speed than it is
Appears to be traveling faster than it is
Stops more quickly than a car
questions.explanation: Because of its large size, a tractor-trailer often appears to be traveling at a slower speed than it is.
questions.sourceQuote: because of its large size, a tractor-trailer often appears to be traveling at a slower speed than it is

questions.question: Large trucks require additional turning room because:
choices: They steer with the rear wheels
They must turn at very low speed
Their rear wheels do not follow the path of their front wheels
questions.explanation: Large trucks require additional turning room because their rear wheels do not follow the path of their front wheels.
questions.sourceQuote: Large trucks require additional turning room because their rear wheels do not follow the path of their front wheels.

questions.question: When following a tractor-trailer that appears to be starting a left turn, you should:
choices: Pass it on the left immediately
Assume it is signaling a right turn
Check which way the driver is signaling before you attempt to pass
questions.explanation: Observe the tractor-trailer's turn signals before trying to pass. If it appears to be starting a left turn, check which way the driver is signaling before you attempt to pass.
questions.sourceQuote: check to see which way the driver is signaling before you attempt to pass

questions.question: Truck brakes create heat when the truck is traveling downhill. This condition:
choices: Has no effect on stopping distance
Allows the truck to gain speed
Requires additional stopping distance for the truck
questions.explanation: Truck brakes create heat when the truck is traveling downhill, and this condition requires additional stopping distance for the truck.
questions.sourceQuote: Truck brakes create heat when the truck is traveling downhill. This condition requires additional stopping distance for the truck.

questions.question: A truck's NO-ZONE blind spot can extend up to how far in front of the cab?
questions.explanation: A car can disappear from the trucker's view up to 20 feet in front of the cab, on either side of the tractor-trailer, and up to 200 feet in the rear.
questions.sourceQuote: 20 feet in front of the cab, on either side of the tractor-trailer, particularly alongside the cab, and up to 200 feet in the rear

questions.question: A truck's NO-ZONE blind spot can extend up to how far behind the trailer?
questions.explanation: The NO-ZONE extends up to 200 feet in the rear of the tractor-trailer.
questions.sourceQuote: up to 200 feet in the rear

questions.question: A general rule for motorists sharing the road with a tractor-trailer is:
choices: If you can't see the truck driver in their side-view mirror, they can't see you
Truck drivers sit high enough to see everything around them
Staying in the truck's blind spot keeps you visible
Pass trucks only on the right
questions.explanation: The general rule is, if you can't see the truck driver in their side-view mirror, they can't see you. Motorists lingering in NO-ZONES hamper the trucker's ability to take evasive action.
questions.sourceQuote: if you can’t see the truck driver in their side-view mirror, they can’t see you

questions.question: Compared with passenger cars, recreational vehicles and trailers:
choices: Accelerate and stop more slowly and require more room for turning
questions.explanation: Most recreational vehicles, including motor homes, campers and travel trailers, are longer, higher and wider than passenger cars, and they accelerate and stop more slowly and require more room for turning.
questions.sourceQuote: Recreational vehicles and trailers accelerate and stop more slowly than cars and require more room for turning.

questions.question: As you approach a recreational vehicle, what happens to your field of vision?
choices: The closer you are, the more the recreational vehicle blocks your view
questions.explanation: Visibility is a major problem with recreational vehicles. The closer you are as you approach one, the more it will block your field of vision.
questions.sourceQuote: the closer you are as you approach a recreational vehicle, the more it will block your field of vision

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle towing a trailer, sudden braking might:
questions.explanation: Be aware that sudden braking might cause the trailer to jackknife when you approach a vehicle towing a trailer.
questions.sourceQuote: sudden braking might cause the trailer to jackknife

questions.question: Safely passing a trailer and the towing vehicle may require:
choices: Half a mile of clear roadway
A quarter mile of clear roadway
questions.explanation: Use extreme caution while passing a trailer and the towing vehicle. It may take you a half mile of clear roadway to safely pass.
questions.sourceQuote: it may take you a half mile of clear roadway to safely pass

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
choices: The right half of the lane
The full width of their lane
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of their lane.
questions.sourceQuote: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of their lane.

questions.question: To pass a motorcycle, you must:
choices: Share its lane with the rider
Change lanes and pass in the same manner as you would for a larger motor vehicle
questions.explanation: To pass a motorcycle, you must change lanes and pass in the same manner as you would for a larger motor vehicle.
questions.sourceQuote: To pass a motorcycle, you must change lanes and pass in the same manner as you would for a larger motor vehicle

questions.question: To pass a moped, you must stay at least:
questions.explanation: A moped should travel using the right side of the lane. To pass a moped, you must stay at least two feet to the left.
questions.sourceQuote: To pass a moped, you must stay at least two feet to the left

questions.question: When passing a cyclist, you must leave enough room so that:
choices: Your horn does not startle the rider
Your vehicle's windstream cannot cause the rider to lose control
The rider cannot draft behind you
questions.explanation: You must leave any cyclist enough room when you pass so your vehicle's windstream cannot cause the rider to lose control.
questions.sourceQuote: your vehicle’s windstream cannot cause the rider to lose control

questions.question: About what portion of motorcycle crashes in North Carolina involve a car?
questions.explanation: About two-thirds of motorcycle crashes in North Carolina involve a car, and in most of these crashes the driver of the car is at fault.
questions.sourceQuote: About two-thirds of motorcycle crashes in North Carolina involve a car.

questions.question: Moped riders and all passengers are required to wear:
choices: A helmet with a retention strap properly secured
questions.explanation: Moped riders and all passengers are required to wear a helmet with a retention strap properly secured.
questions.sourceQuote: Moped riders and all passengers are required to wear a helmet with a retention strap properly secured.

questions.question: A moped helmet must comply with:
questions.explanation: The helmet must be a type that complies with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS 218).
questions.sourceQuote: The helmet must be a type that complies with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS 218).

questions.question: Compared with cars, most motorcycles:
choices: Stop more slowly in all conditions
Can stop more quickly, but stop more slowly with a second rider or on poor road surfaces
Cannot stop as quickly under any condition
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles can stop more quickly than cars, but they stop more slowly when there is a second rider or when traveling on poor road surfaces.
questions.sourceQuote: Most can stop more quickly than cars, but motorcycles stop more slowly when there is a second rider or when traveling on poor road surfaces

questions.question: In North Carolina, a moped is defined as a vehicle with:
choices: Two wheels and a motor of no more than 250 cubic centimeters
Four wheels and a motor of no more than 50 cubic centimeters
Two or three wheels, a motor of no more than 50 cubic centimeters, and no external shifting device
Any two-wheeled vehicle with a motor
questions.explanation: A moped is defined as a vehicle with two or three wheels with a motor of no more than 50 cubic centimeters of piston displacement and no external shifting device.
questions.sourceQuote: a vehicle with two or three wheels with a motor of no more than 50 cubic centimeters of piston displacement and no external shifting device

questions.question: By law, a moped's top speed cannot exceed:
questions.explanation: Legally, a moped's top speed cannot exceed 30 miles per hour.
questions.sourceQuote: Legally, a moped’s top speed cannot exceed 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: To operate a moped on a public roadway in North Carolina, you must be at least:
questions.explanation: In North Carolina you must be at least 16 years old to operate a moped on a public roadway or public vehicular area.
questions.sourceQuote: In North Carolina you must be at least 16 years old to operate a moped on a public roadway or public vehicular area.

questions.question: The cost of registering a moped is:
questions.explanation: The cost of registering each moped is $29.50 annually. Some counties charge an additional transit tax.
questions.sourceQuote: The cost of registering each moped is $29.50 annually.

questions.question: If litter is thrown from or blown from a vehicle, who is held responsible?
questions.explanation: When litter is thrown from or blown from a vehicle, the driver of the vehicle is held responsible.
questions.sourceQuote: When litter is thrown from or blown from a vehicle, the driver of the vehicle is held responsible.

questions.question: For a first conviction of littering, the fine is:
questions.explanation: If convicted of littering, the minimum fine is $250 and the maximum fine is $1,000.
questions.sourceQuote: the minimum fine is $250, and the maximum fine is $1,000

questions.question: A second or subsequent littering offense within three years of a prior offense is punishable by a fine of:
questions.explanation: Any second or subsequent offense within three years after the date of a prior offense is punishable by a fine of not less than $500 nor more than $2,000.
questions.sourceQuote: punishable by a fine of not less than $500 nor more than $2,000

questions.question: To join the Adopt-A-Highway program, a group agrees to pick up litter:
choices: Once a year along a two-mile section
At least four times a year along a two-mile section
questions.explanation: A group agrees to pick up litter at least four times a year along a two-mile section of state-maintained roadway.
questions.sourceQuote: agrees to pick up litter at least four times a year along a two–mile section of state–maintained roadway

questions.question: What must be completed before you can obtain a copy of your driving record from the DMV?
choices: The Driver Privacy Protection Act Request Form (DL-DPPA-I)
questions.explanation: The Driver Privacy Protection Act Request Form (DL-DPPA-I) must be completed before your driving record can be obtained. The form is available at DMV Headquarters and on the DMV website.
questions.sourceQuote: The Driver Privacy Protection Act Request Form (DL-DPPA-I), available at DMV Headquarters and on the DMV website

questions.question: What is the fee for a certified copy of a North Carolina driving record?
questions.explanation: A certified copy of a driving record costs $18 and is available online. The non-certified records cost $12.75.
questions.sourceQuote: $18 for certified copy of record (available online)

questions.question: What is required before you can title or register a vehicle in North Carolina?
questions.explanation: A North Carolina driver license is required prior to titling or registering a vehicle in this state.
questions.sourceQuote: A North Carolina driver license is required prior to titling/registering a vehicle in this State.

questions.question: The registration card for a vehicle must be:
choices: mailed to the DMV each year
kept in the vehicle at all times
stored with the certificate of title
questions.explanation: The registration card must be kept in the vehicle at all times and must always be available to show a law enforcement officer upon request.
questions.sourceQuote: The registration card must be kept in the vehicle at all times

questions.question: Which of these is prohibited on a vehicle in North Carolina?
choices: A validation sticker on the license plate
An expiration decal on the plate
A registration card in the vehicle
questions.explanation: Plastic license plate covers are prohibited under General Statute 20-63g.
questions.sourceQuote: Plastic license plate covers are prohibited. GS 20-63g.

questions.question: Within how many days of moving within North Carolina must a license or ID holder update their physical address with the DMV?
questions.explanation: Within 60 days of moving within North Carolina, a license or ID holder must update their physical address with the DMV and get a duplicate license or ID.
questions.sourceQuote: Within 60 days of moving within North Carolina, a license or ID holder must update their physical address with the DMV

questions.question: For a new vehicle, which document serves as the official transfer document?
questions.explanation: For new vehicles, the manufacturer's certificate of origin is the official transfer document required as proof of ownership.
questions.sourceQuote: For new vehicles, the manufacturer's certificate of origin is the official transfer document

questions.question: You purchase a used vehicle that has already been registered. What must you present when registering it?
choices: A notarized bill of sale only
The certificate of title properly assigned by the former owner
questions.explanation: For a used vehicle that has already been registered, you must present the certificate of title properly assigned by the former owner.
questions.sourceQuote: must present the certificate of title properly assigned by the former owner

questions.question: Which situation allows a valid out-of-state driver license to be accepted for a vehicle registration in North Carolina?
choices: Military active duty stationed in North Carolina
Living in North Carolina for 10 years
Paying the registration fee in cash
questions.explanation: Out-of-state licenses or IDs may be accepted with documentation such as military active duty stationed in North Carolina, school enrollment in North Carolina, or a vehicle garaged in the state for a minimum of six months.
questions.sourceQuote: Valid driver licenses or identification cards issued by other states may be accepted for vehicle registrations

questions.question: What is the minimum liability insurance required for injuries to any one person in a crash in North Carolina?
questions.explanation: The minimum amount of liability insurance required is $30,000 for injuries to any one person in a crash.
questions.sourceQuote: $30,000 for injuries to any one person in a crash

questions.question: If the DMV is notified that an owner is operating a vehicle without proper liability insurance, the license plate could be revoked for how long?
questions.explanation: The license plate could be revoked for 30 days unless proof of continuous insurance coverage is provided.
questions.sourceQuote: could be revoked for 30 days unless proof of continuous insurance coverage is provided

questions.question: Does North Carolina honor a grace period for lapsed liability insurance?
choices: No, North Carolina does not honor a grace period
Yes, a six month grace period
questions.explanation: North Carolina does not honor a grace period. A grace period is an agreement between the insured and the insurance company only.
questions.sourceQuote: North Carolina does not honor a grace period.

questions.question: To avoid a fine or penalty, what should you do before terminating or canceling liability insurance on a vehicle?
choices: Surrender the vehicle's valid license plate
questions.explanation: Surrender a vehicle's valid license plate prior to the termination or cancellation of liability insurance to avoid a fine or penalty.
questions.sourceQuote: surrender a vehicle's valid license plate prior to the termination or cancellation of liability insurance

questions.question: All self-propelled vehicles must receive a safety or safety and emission inspection within how many days prior to the registration expiration to renew their registration?
questions.explanation: Within 90 days prior to the registration expiration, all self-propelled vehicles are required to receive a safety or safety and emission inspection to renew their registration.
questions.sourceQuote: Within 90 days prior to the registration expiration

questions.question: When ownership of a vehicle is transferred, the reassignment on the certificate of title must be made in the presence of whom?
questions.explanation: Reassignment of ownership is made using section A on side two of the certificate of title, and it must be made in the presence of a Notary Public for the transfer to be valid.
questions.sourceQuote: the reassignment must be made in the presence of a Notary Public

questions.question: License plates can be transferred from one vehicle to another of the same category provided that:
choices: both vehicles are the same model year
the vehicles are registered in different states
ownership is in the same name and insurance coverage has been continuous
a new inspection is completed within 30 days
questions.explanation: Plates can be transferred between vehicles of the same category if ownership is in the same name and insurance coverage has been continuous.
questions.sourceQuote: License plates can be transferred from one vehicle to another of the same category

questions.question: How long after the application and fee are received by the DMV can a duplicate title be issued?
questions.explanation: A duplicate title cannot be issued until 15 days after the application and fee are received by the DMV.
questions.sourceQuote: A duplicate title cannot be issued until 15 days after the application and fee are received by the DMV

questions.question: Under the Tag & Tax Together program, how are the license tag renewal and the vehicle property tax paid?
choices: Only at the county tax office
questions.explanation: The Tag & Tax Together program requires one payment for both bills, and both must be paid in full to renew a vehicle's annual registration.
questions.sourceQuote: The “Tag & Tax Together” program requires one payment for both bills.

questions.question: A vehicle that fails inspection is entitled to be re-inspected at the same station within how many days without paying another inspection fee?
questions.explanation: A vehicle that fails inspection may be re-inspected at the same station within 60 days without paying another inspection fee.
questions.sourceQuote: A vehicle that fails inspection is entitled to be re-inspected at the same station within 60 days

questions.question: Vehicles with less than 70,000 miles and within the three most recent model years will receive which type of inspection?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with less than 70,000 miles and within the three most recent model years will receive a safety only inspection.
questions.sourceQuote: Vehicles with less than 70,000 miles and within the “three most recent model years” will receive a safety only inspection

questions.question: What is the minimum allowable light transmittance for after-factory tinted windows in North Carolina?
questions.explanation: The allowable light transmittance for tinted windows is no less than 35%.
questions.sourceQuote: The allowable light transmittance for tinted windows is no less than 35%.

questions.question: Vehicles with after-factory window tinting are charged what additional fee as part of the vehicle inspection?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with after-factory window tinting are charged an additional fee of $10 as part of the vehicle inspection.
questions.sourceQuote: Vehicles with after-factory window tinting will be charged an additional fee of $10 as part of the vehicle inspection
